title: Deluge
descript: Deluge is a lightweight BitTorrent client with a full web interface. Add torrents, watch progress and manage seeds from any browser on your network while the daemon keeps running in the container. This package runs the official LinuxServer.io Deluge image as a non-root container; its configuration and downloaded files live in the application data folder. The default web password is deluge; change it on first login.
important: Requires DockerEngine. The default web password is 'deluge' - change it immediately. Only the web port is published, so incoming peer connections rely on UPnP/NAT-PMP or router port forwarding; downloads still work with outgoing connections. Files are stored in DockerAppData/delugedocker (config and downloads) and are not shared with other apps. Back up the folder before uninstalling with data removal. The page is plain HTTP on the LAN.
release_note: 1. First release: Deluge 2.2.0 from Docker Hub, running as a non-root container; configuration and downloads live in the application data folder.

data_notes: `config` holds the daemon and web settings; `downloads` holds the torrent data. Copying `config` keeps the client configuration; the downloads folder is your own data.
design_notes: **Runs as a non-root container.** Verified on real hardware as uid 1000.
**Two volumes.** `/config` keeps the daemon/web settings; `/downloads` receives the torrent data.
**Health check** probes the web UI on container port 8112.
**Fixed image tag, never `:latest`**, Docker Hub only, no `privileged`, no `network_mode: host`, no Docker socket, no `cap_add`.
limitations: Only the web UI port is published. Incoming peer connections need UPnP/NAT-PMP or router port forwarding; outgoing connections still download.
`/downloads` belongs to this app only and is not shared with the Radarr/Sonarr/Lidarr packages.
No VPN is included. Use a VPN or a trusted network if your torrent traffic must be private.
The page is plain HTTP on the LAN; use a TLS reverse proxy before exposing it to the internet, and change the default password immediately.
Docker applications cannot be upgraded in place in the App Center: updating means uninstalling and reinstalling, which keeps the data folders.
